walkthroughs.body_html:
Two words that look similar but mean different things.

Validity = are you measuring the right thing? If your water heats up under the lamp, you've changed two factors (light AND temperature) — the test is invalid. Fix it with a heat-shield beaker of water between lamp and pondweed.

Reliability = do repeats agree? Repeating reduces random error; controls remove confounders.

Don't lose easy marks on graph choice.

Line graph — use when BOTH axes show continuous numerical data (e.g. distance vs bubbles/min).

Bar chart — use when the x-axis is categorical (e.g. comparing pondweed, geranium, fern).

Top tips: label axes with quantity AND units, plot points with a small cross or dot, draw a smooth line of best fit (not dot-to-dot).

A full required-practical answer should hit these points:

Independent variable: distance of lamp from pondweed.

Dependent variable: bubbles per minute (or volume of O₂ per minute).

Control variables: temperature (use heat-shield), CO₂ (sodium hydrogencarbonate), same pondweed, same lamp wattage, same time interval.

Repeats: at least 3 per distance, then take a mean and ignore anomalies.

Limitation: bubbles vary in size, so collecting volume of oxygen in a measuring cylinder is more accurate.
